events.title: The future Emperor Augustus is born in Rome
events.description: Gaius Octavius was born in Rome, great-nephew of Julius Caesar. As Augustus he ended the civil wars and turned the Republic into a monarchy that lasted for centuries.

events.title: John Paul Jones captures HMS Serapis off Flamborough Head
events.description: In a brutal moonlit battle, John Paul Jones's sinking Bonhomme Richard captured HMS Serapis off Yorkshire. His later-reported reply 'I have not yet begun to fight' became a naval legend.

events.title: Johann Galle discovers Neptune
events.description: At the Berlin Observatory, Johann Galle found Neptune within a degree of where Urbain Le Verrier had calculated. It was the first planet found by mathematical prediction.

events.title: Sigmund Freud dies in London
events.description: Freud, who had fled Nazi-occupied Vienna the year before, died aged 83 after his doctor gave him lethal doses of morphine at his request. His theories of the unconscious reshaped twentieth-century thought.
